question: In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin intervene (n):
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: The TAP proteins -> transport peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum -> aid in peptide loading onto MHC class I molecules -> 80% CHAIN: The tapasina -> assists in the assembly of MHC class II molecules -> facilitates peptide binding -> 75% CHAIN: The HLA-DM molecule -> acts as a chaperone for MHC class II molecules -> helps in peptide exchange -> 70% CHAIN: The proteasome -> degrades intracellular proteins into peptides -> generates antigenic peptides for presentation -> 85% CHAIN: The HLA-B molecules -> present peptides to cytotoxic T cells -> initiate immune response -> 80%
analysis: In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin, the TAP proteins play a crucial role in transporting peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I molecules. The tapasina, HLA-DM molecule, and HLA-B molecules are also involved in antigen presentation, but they are not specifically related to peptides of extracellular origin. The proteasome is involved in the degradation of intracellular proteins for antigen presentation.
